summary: Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University (~1975–1986, PhD). In sinology and international relations, he served at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Linguist Eberhard Schrader studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen (~1854–1858). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1863–1870), University of Giessen (~1870–1873), University of Jena (~1873–1875), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

Active in Indology and philosophy, Edeltraud Harzer studied at Charles University, the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Sri Narayana Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

Linguist Edgar Howard Sturtevant studied at Illinois College (1893–1895) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1895–1898). His career included posts at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).
Edgar Polomé studied at Université catholique de Louvain (~1945–1949). In linguistics and Indology, he served as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1993–2000).

Edgar Thurston studied at Eton College (~1869–1874) and King's College London (~1874–1877). Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1885–1908).

Specializing in philosophy and religious studies, Edith Wyschogrod studied at Hunter College (~1947–1951) and Columbia University (~1964–1970). She served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Working in religious studies and sinology, Edmond Yee held faculty posts attested in 2003 at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

In Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Edmund Hardy studied at Mainz, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), Berlin, and Freiburg. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1885–1893), University of Fribourg (1894–1898), and University of Würzburg (~1894–1904).

Philosopher Edmund Husserl studied under Wilhelm Wundt at Leipzig, as well as at Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and University of Freiburg (1916–1928).

Edmund Leach studied at Cambridge and the London School of Economics (PhD). Working in religious studies and related fields, he held posts at the LSE (~1947–1953), Cambridge (1953–1978), King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979), and the Royal Anthropological Institute (1971–1975).
Indologist Edmund Nathaniel Snyder graduated from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Edo Shonin is attested in 2015 as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.
Linguist Eduard Böhmer studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1845–1849). He later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig (~1908–1913) under August Conrady. He later held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1951–1958).

Specialist in linguistics and Indology Eduard Hermann studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena (PhD under Berthold Delbrück). He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917–1937), joining the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1918.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Eduard Müller completed his Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1871–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

Indologist and philosopher Eduard Röer studied under Johann Friedrich Herbart and Franz Bopp at Königsberg and Jena. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833), the East India Company (~1839–1858), and The Asiatic Society from 1841.

Eduard Sachau studied at Kiel under Theodor Nöldeke, Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus and Heinrich Fleischer, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD). He worked in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies at Vienna (1869), Berlin (from 1876), and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).
Working in linguistics and Indology, Eduard Schwyzer held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1912–1927), the University of Bonn (~1927–1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1943).
